subject: General English
tone_notes: The tone is formal and academic, appropriate for A-Level examinations. Vocabulary level is advanced. Passages typically include factual texts (news items, research findings, social commentary), short narratives, poems, and data representations (bar charts). Questions are direct and require precise answers, adherence to word limits, and correct grammar/punctuation. Formatting often includes numbered questions, lettered/roman numeral options for multiple-choice, and clearly marked blanks.
instructions_pattern: Answer all questions on this paper itself.
Marks will be deducted for bad punctuation (Omission of full stops, capital letters, etc.) and for mistakes in basic grammar.
The supervisor will provide you with sheets for rough work.
Use additional reading time to go through the question paper and decide on the questions that you give priority in answering.

sections.title: PART A - READING SKILLS
sections.instructions: Read the following texts and poems carefully and answer the questions that follow, using the provided information and inferring where necessary.

sections.title: PART B - DIALOGUES
sections.instructions: Respond appropriately to given situations, or complete and create dialogues as instructed, adhering to specified sentence limits.
sections.typical_prompt_style: How do you respond in each of the following situations? Write only one sentence or question for each, beginning with the word/s given.; Complete the following dialogue between [BLANK] and [BLANK]. Do not use more than two sentences/ questions in each blank.; Imagine that you [BLANK]. Write out the dialogue between your friend and you. Each one should speak at least five times.

sections.title: PART C - WRITING SKILLS
sections.instructions: Demonstrate writing proficiency through various tasks including sentence construction, data description, and extended writing forms such as emails, letters, and essays.
